facts.value: Culture and religion have usually been seen as closely related. Paul Tillich looked at religion as the soul of culture and culture as the form or framework of religion.

Religion as ultimate concern is the meaning-giving substance of culture, and culture is the totality of forms in which the basic concern of religion expresses itself. In abbreviation: religion is the substance of culture, culture is the form of religion.
Culture as the soil of religion; transplanting a religion from its original culture to a foreign culture would kill it.
Many attempts in the modern pluralistic situation to distinguish culture from religion.
Elements grounded on beliefs of a metaphysical nature (religious) are distinct from elements grounded on nature and the natural (cultural).
Language (with its grammar) is a cultural element while sacralization of language in which a particular religious scripture is written is more often a religious practice.
Criticism of religion includes the criticism of ideas, truth, or the practice of religion, including its political and social implications.
